items.title: CVE-2026-100725 (HIGH 8.3): http4k (Maven artifact org.http4k:http4k-core) before 6.48.0.0, 5.42.0.0, and 4.51.0.0 ships a BasicCookieSto…
items.one_liner: CVE-2026-100725 is an 8.3-rated cookie scoping vulnerability in http4k that leaks session tokens across different origins.
items.summary: A high-severity security vulnerability has been identified in the http4k core library across Maven artifact versions before 6.48.0.0, 5.42.0.0, and 4.51.0.0, tracked as CVE-2026-100725 with a CVSS base score of 8.3. The flaw exists within BasicCookieStorage—the client-side cookie store utilized by ClientFilters.Cookies—which fails to enforce proper RFC 6265 scoping rules concerning cookie domains, paths, and Secure attributes. When a single cookie storage instance interacts with multiple origins or communication schemes, cookies designated for one origin can be improperly sent to unauthorized hosts or transmitted in plain text over HTTP. This exposes sensitive session tokens and values to network observers, though clients utilizing dedicated storage instances for single origins remain unaffected.
items.bottom_line: Applications using shared http4k BasicCookieStorage instances across multiple origins risk leaking session cookies to unauthorized hosts and observers.

claims.text: CVE-2026-100725 (HIGH 8.3): http4k (Maven artifact org.http4k:http4k-core) before 6.48.0.0, 5.42.0.0, and 4.51.0.0 ships a BasicCookieStorage (client-side cookie store used by ClientFilters.Cookies) that does not enforce RFC 6265 scoping rules for the cookie domain, path, and Secure attributes.

items.title: Beyond Semantic Narrowing: Robust and Efficient LLM Watermarking with Hamming Neighborhoods
items.one_liner: HammingMark improves LLM watermarking efficiency and quality by validating tokens within Hamming neighborhoods in compact hash space.
items.summary: Semantic watermarking embeds detectable signals into LLM-generated text to resist removal attacks, but often suffers from semantic narrowing due to poor alignment with natural generation preferences. To solve this, researchers introduced HammingMark, which uses semantic hashes of preceding sentences to accept candidate tokens falling within a dynamic Hamming neighborhood. Experiments on C4 and BookSum datasets show that HammingMark achieves strong robustness and high detectability while requiring only 2.2 sampled candidates per sentence—a 72.8 percent reduction over existing methods.
items.bottom_line: Hamming-neighborhood semantic hashing eliminates semantic narrowing in LLM watermarks while cutting resampling overhead by nearly 73 percent.

claims.text: Experiments on C4 and BookSum show that HammingMark achieves strong robustness, high detectability, and near-unwatermarked generation quality, requiring only 2.2 sampled candidates per sentence,a 72.8% reduction compared with the most sampling-efficient existing method.

items.title: pikit: A Composable Toolkit for Indirect Prompt Injection Research and Evaluation
items.one_liner: pikit is a new composable research toolkit designed to evaluate indirect prompt injection vectors, attack channels, and defense strategies on LLM agents.
items.summary: Researchers have released pikit, an open-source, composable research toolkit built to systematically evaluate indirect prompt injection threats across LLM-based agent environments. The framework integrates 13 attack methods, 16 communication channels spanning text and file vectors, and 9 prevention strategies alongside offline detection baselines. Using a decorator-based registry and a unified craft() API, pikit allows security researchers to compose arbitrary attacks and test defenses seamlessly. Benchmarking 9 prevention controls on a production-like coding agent demonstrated a 71.8% relative reduction in attack success rates, with instruction hierarchy and few-shot warnings providing the most robust defense.
items.bottom_line: Security teams can use pikit to benchmark LLM agent resilience against indirect prompt injections and test multi-layered prevention strategies.

items.title: Render Before Reading: Visual Rendering as a Prompt Injection Defense
items.one_liner: Rendering untrusted input as images is an effective, training-free defense against prompt injection in multimodal LLMs.
items.summary: Research into prompt injection defenses identifies a 'modality gap' where multimodal LLMs are more susceptible to adversarial text instructions than the same instructions delivered via images. The authors propose 'Pictionary,' a training-free defense that renders untrusted payloads as images before processing, which consistently reduces attack success rates across multiple benchmarks. This approach leverages the model's inherent bias toward treating non-textual modalities as content rather than instructions.
items.bottom_line: If you are building multimodal agent pipelines, consider rendering untrusted user inputs as images before passing them to the LLM to mitigate prompt injection risks.

claims.text: Multimodal LLMs are more likely to follow adversarial instruction when they appear as text than when the same instruction is delivered through a non-textual channel.
claims.support_span: multimodal LLMs are more likely to follow adversarial instruction when they appear as text than when the same instruction is delivered through a non-textual channel (e.g., as an image).

claims.text: We demonstrate how this gap can be turned into a training-free defense, by rendering all untrusted payloads as typographic images (or audio) before they reach the model.
claims.support_span: We demonstrate how this gap can be turned into a training-free defense, by rendering all untrusted payloads as typographic images (or audio) before they reach the model.

items.title: Principled Thoughts for Latent Recursive LLM Systems
items.one_liner: REST (REpresentation-Supervised Thoughts) improves LLM reasoning accuracy and interpretability by adding representation losses to latent thoughts.
items.summary: Large language models reasoning in continuous space via hidden states often suffer from failures under standard Cross-Entropy (CE) training, such as collapsing thoughts across distinct questions and retaining irrelevant information. To resolve these issues, researchers introduce REST (REpresentation-Supervised Thoughts), a training objective that translates four valid thought representation properties—causality, minimality, separability, and stability—into differentiable loss functions added to CE. Implemented across single-agent and multi-agent systems without adding parameters at inference, REST increases task accuracy by up to 7.5 percentage points and answer convergence by 30% across seven benchmarks spanning math, science, and code generation.
key_facts: Accuracy improvement: Up to 7.5 percentage points
items.bottom_line: REST optimizes latent LLM reasoning spaces by enforcing causality, minimality, separability, and stability, boosting accuracy by up to 7.5%.

claims.text: We introduce REST (REpresentation-Supervised Thoughts), a training objective that turns four properties of a valid thought representation into differentiable losses added to CE.
claims.support_span: We introduce REST (REpresentation-Supervised Thoughts), a training objective that turns four properties of a valid thought representation (causality, minimality, separability, and stability) into differentiable losses added to CE.

claims.text: REST increases accuracy over CE-only training across agent settings and model sizes by up to 7.5 percentage points and convergence on a final answer by 30%.
claims.support_span: Across 7 benchmarks spanning mathematics, science, medicine, and code generation, with the same training data, compute, and latent budget, REST increases accuracy over CE-only training across agent settings and model sizes by up to 7.5 percentage points and convergence on a final answer by 30%.

items.title: USN-8845-1: GVfs vulnerabilities
items.one_liner: GVfs vulnerabilities on Ubuntu enable SFTP-based code execution and local root privilege escalation via D-Bus socket ownership changes.
items.summary: Ubuntu published a security advisory detailing vulnerabilities in GVfs affecting versions on Ubuntu 22.04 LTS, 24.04 LTS, and 26.04 LTS. A heap buffer overflow vulnerability in SFTP server data validation (CVE-2026-84268) can be exploited to achieve arbitrary code execution or denial of service. Additionally, an improper file ownership handling flaw in private D-Bus socket creation within the admin backend (CVE-2026-88924) allows local attackers to change ownership of arbitrary system files, resulting in root privilege escalation.
key_facts: CVE-2026-84268: SFTP heap buffer overflow for code execution/DoS
CVE-2026-88924: Admin backend D-Bus socket file ownership root escalation
Affected releases: Ubuntu 22.04 LTS, 24.04 LTS, 26.04 LTS
items.bottom_line: Unvalidated SFTP data and insecure D-Bus socket handling in GVfs allow local attackers to achieve root escalation or remote code execution.

claims.text: A local attacker could possibly use this issue to change the ownership of arbitrary system files, resulting in privilege escalation to root. (CVE-2026-88924)
claims.support_span: A local attacker could possibly use this issue to change the ownership of arbitrary system files, resulting in privilege escalation to root. (CVE-2026-88924)
